couplets.gloss: Someone who can tell what you are thinking before you say a word is a gift to the whole world.

edges.reason: Calls the man who knows a thought before it is voiced an ornament to all the world.
edges.quote: look and know what is meant, with nothing said

edges.reason: Such a reader of minds is worn by the whole world like a jewel.
edges.quote: an ornament to the world

couplets.gloss: Treat anyone who can see into another person's heart, without any doubt, as if they were a god.

edges.reason: Rates certainty about another’s heart so high that its owner is held the equal of a god.
edges.quote: knows without doubt what is in another’s heart

couplets.gloss: People who can work out someone's intentions from their expression are worth bringing on board at any price.

edges.reason: Says those who can read a thought from its signs are worth having at any cost.
edges.quote: gain those who can read a thought from its signs

edges.reason: Speaks to someone with a council to fill, which makes this a ruler's advice.
edges.quote: take them into thy council

couplets.gloss: People who grasp things without being told may look like everyone else, but they are a different breed.

edges.reason: Though they look like anyone else, those who understand without words are counted a kind apart.
edges.quote: Those who grasp a thought unspoken

couplets.gloss: If the eye cannot pick up from a glance what is in someone's heart, what good is it among the senses?

edges.reason: Holds that eyes unable to read a thought have no use among the parts of the body.
edges.quote: eyes can’t read a thought from its signs

edges.reason: Measures the eye by what it can understand and not by what it can see.
edges.quote: what use are they among the body’s parts

couplets.gloss: A face shows what someone feels inside, just as clear crystal picks up the colour of whatever sits beside it.

edges.reason: Gives the ground of the art: the face takes the heart's colour as crystal takes a neighbour's.
edges.quote: the face shows what is strongest in the heart

couplets.gloss: Nothing gives you away like your face: whether you are pleased or furious, it shows there before anywhere else.

edges.reason: Anger and gladness reach the face first, which makes it the first place to read a heart.
edges.quote: In gladness or in anger, it gets there first

couplets.gloss: If you find someone who understands what is going on inside you without being told, you only have to stand before them.

edges.reason: With someone who can read your heart, you need say nothing: standing before them is enough.
edges.quote: look within and know what has happened to you

couplets.gloss: To someone who knows how eyes work, the eyes alone reveal whether a person feels hatred or friendship.

edges.reason: For those who know its ways, the eye alone tells enmity from friendship.
edges.quote: The eyes themselves will tell enmity and friendship

couplets.gloss: Ask what truly perceptive people use to size someone up, and it turns out to be nothing but their own eyes.

edges.reason: Whoever claims subtlety has only his eye to gauge another's mind.
edges.quote: no measuring rod but the eye

edges.reason: The eye becomes a rod held up against other men's minds.
edges.quote: measuring rod

couplets.gloss: If you know the value of words, find out who you are talking to and fit what you say to them.

edges.reason: Tells the skilled speaker to study the assembly and weigh it before saying anything.
edges.quote: know the assembly, weigh it up, and then speak

edges.reason: Calls directly on those who know the range of words and must stand before a gathering.
edges.quote: who know the range of words

edges.reason: Gives anyone facing a room a first step: learn who is in it before deciding what to say.
edges.quote: know the assembly

couplets.gloss: If you speak well, check the mood of the room first and think it through before you open your mouth.

edges.reason: Puts judging the moment ahead of any speech, however good the speaker.
edges.quote: judge the moment

edges.reason: Calls directly on those who have studied the ways of words.
edges.quote: good at the ways of words

couplets.gloss: People who stand up to speak without sizing up the crowd do not understand speaking and are not much use at anything else.

edges.reason: Those who speak without weighing the assembly know nothing of speech and are fit for little else.
edges.quote: without knowing the assembly

edges.reason: Passes judgment on anyone who takes it on himself to speak to a gathering.
edges.quote: take on speaking without knowing the assembly

couplets.gloss: Be brilliant among the brilliant, but with fools answer only at the level they can follow.

edges.reason: Fits you to the hearers: bright before the bright, and blank as white lime before the blank.
edges.quote: Be bright before the bright

edges.reason: Advises not spending your brightness on those who can’t take it in, only going as blank as they are.
edges.quote: Before the blank, take on the colour of white lime

couplets.gloss: Holding back from speaking first among your elders is a discipline that beats even other good qualities.

edges.reason: Ranks the restraint of not speaking first among elders above other virtues.
edges.quote: the restraint of not speaking first among elders

couplets.gloss: Slipping up in front of wise, well-read people is as bad as straying from the right path.

edges.reason: A slip before the discerning is as grave as leaving the right road, so such hearers call for care.
edges.quote: A failure before men of understanding

couplets.gloss: A scholar's learning only really shows when it is put before people who can spot every flaw.

edges.reason: Learning shines out before hearers able to weigh words without fault.
edges.quote: shines among those who can weigh words without fault

edges.reason: Concerns the scholar, whose learning shines among those who can weigh words.
edges.quote: The learning of the well-read

couplets.gloss: Explaining something to people able to understand it is like watering plants that are already growing.

edges.reason: Speech given to those who can take it in feeds them, as water feeds what is already growing.
edges.quote: To speak before those with understanding

edges.reason: Speaking to people of understanding is water poured on a bed of growing plants.
edges.quote: pouring water on a bed where something is already growing

couplets.gloss: If you want your words to please wise people, take care never to speak to a crowd of fools, even by accident.

edges.reason: Warns those who speak well before a good assembly not to speak in a petty one, even by forgetting.
edges.quote: don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting

edges.reason: Calls directly on those who can make a good assembly take in what they say.
edges.quote: speak so that a good assembly takes it in

couplets.gloss: Giving a talk to people who are not your kind is like spilling the food of the gods down a drain.

edges.reason: Speaking before those not of your own kind is pure waste, so a speaker must pick the hearers.
edges.quote: before those not of your own kind

edges.reason: Talk before those not of your own kind is the sweetest thing there is, lost in a filthy yard.
edges.quote: ambrosia spilled in a filthy yard

couplets.gloss: People who know the weight of words can arrange what they say and will not slip up in front of a sharp audience.

edges.reason: Those who know their words stand firm and don’t slip before an able gathering.
edges.quote: don’t slip before an able one

edges.reason: Describes speakers who know the range of words and stand before an able assembly.
edges.quote: who know the range of words

couplets.gloss: Whoever can make what they have learned land with other learned people earns the name of the scholar's scholar.

edges.reason: Making the learned take in what you have learned earns the name of learned among the learned.
edges.quote: say what they have learned so that the learned take it in

edges.reason: Concerns those who stand up before a learned gathering and say what they have learned.
edges.quote: so that the learned take it in

couplets.gloss: Plenty of people will die in battle, but very few can stand before an audience without shaking.

edges.reason: Rates calm before an assembly as rarer than the bravery that faces death in war.
edges.quote: Those who have no fear in an assembly are rare

couplets.gloss: Share what you have mastered with those who know, and learn what you lack from those better than you.

edges.reason: Tells the speaker to take what he lacks from those who excel in it.
edges.quote: from those who have learned more, take that more

edges.reason: Directs one who lays his knowledge before a learned company.
edges.quote: Say what you have learned so that the learned take it in

couplets.gloss: Study logic properly so that you can answer back without fear in any gathering.

edges.reason: Fearless answering is the stated goal, and right learning is the training for it.
edges.quote: answer in an assembly without fear

edges.reason: Tells the would-be speaker to learn by the right path before facing a gathering.
edges.quote: so that you can answer in an assembly without fear

edges.reason: Tells a nervous speaker that learning by the right path is what takes the fear away.
edges.quote: Learn by the right path and know the measure

couplets.gloss: What use is a sword to someone with no courage, or books to someone scared of a sharp audience?

edges.reason: Asks what someone without courage wants with a sword at all.
edges.quote: those who lack hard courage

edges.reason: Books are nothing to one who fears an assembly of subtle minds.
edges.quote: those who fear a subtle assembly

edges.reason: Pairs a coward's sword with a timid scholar's books, each useless in its owner's hands.
edges.quote: What has a sword to do with those

couplets.gloss: The learning of someone scared of an audience is as useless as a fine sword held by someone who will never fight.
couplets.sensitive: uses eunuchs as a byword for uselessness

edges.reason: Learning with no nerve behind it can never be put to use.
edges.quote: The learning of a man who fears the assembly

edges.reason: The sword in a eunuch's hand is the emblem of a weapon that will never strike.
edges.quote: a bright sword in a eunuch’s hand

couplets.gloss: However much someone has studied, it is no use if they cannot get their point across to a good audience.

edges.reason: Wide learning counts for nothing in one who can’t make a good assembly take in what is said.
edges.quote: can’t speak so that a good assembly takes it in

edges.reason: Aimed at men of wide study who fail when they have to speak.
edges.quote: however much they have learned

couplets.gloss: Well-read people who are afraid of a learned crowd are thought even less of than people with no education.

edges.reason: Fear of an assembly of the good drops the learned below even the unlearned.
edges.quote: fear an assembly of the good

edges.reason: Speaks of those who have learning yet fear an assembly of the good.
edges.quote: those who have learned and understood

couplets.gloss: People too frightened of a crowd to share what they have learned are alive, but might as well not be.

edges.reason: Fear that keeps learning unspoken leaves a man nothing to show for being alive.
edges.quote: fear the assembly and can’t get across what they have learned

edges.reason: Still alive, those who can’t speak before others are counted among those who are not.
edges.quote: are alive, yet they are like those who are not

couplets.gloss: A great country has harvests that never fail, and is where wise people and decent wealthy people choose to settle.

edges.reason: Measures a land by harvests that never fail and by the worthy and the rich who settle there.
edges.quote: unfailing harvests, worthy people and the rich who never decline

couplets.gloss: A great country draws people in with its riches and grows plenty because nothing blights its crops.

edges.reason: Great wealth makes it desired, and freedom from ruin keeps its fields yielding.
edges.quote: desired for its great wealth

couplets.gloss: A great nation takes on load after load, bears it all and still pays everything it owes to its ruler.

edges.reason: Its greatness shows when every burden falls at once and it still holds up.
edges.quote: bears every burden that falls on it at once

edges.reason: The country here is its people, who bear the load and still pay the ruler in full.
edges.quote: gives its ruler his whole tax

couplets.gloss: A great country has no famine, no epidemics and no enemies breaking in.

edges.reason: Names three things a country is spared: deep hunger, endless sickness and destroying enemies.
edges.quote: free of deep hunger, endless sickness and destroying enemies

couplets.gloss: A great nation is not split into feuding factions and has no violent gangs or traitors tearing it apart from inside.

edges.reason: Greatness here is unity: no rival factions and no murderous rebels loose inside the realm.
edges.quote: no rival factions

edges.reason: Counts enemies inside the country among what would ruin it.
edges.quote: no ruinous enemies within

couplets.gloss: The best country is one enemies have never wrecked, and which would lose none of its productivity even if they did.

edges.reason: Crowns the land that escapes ruin and whose riches hold even if ruin comes.
edges.quote: knows no ruin, and whose riches hold even when it is ruined

couplets.gloss: Every country needs water from above and below ground, well-placed hills and strong defences.

edges.reason: Names the limbs of a country: its waters, its hill and its strong fortress.
edges.quote: are the limbs of a country

edges.reason: Lists rainwater among the waters no land can do without.
edges.quote: rainwater

edges.reason: Closes the list of a country’s limbs with a strong fortress.
edges.quote: a strong fortress

couplets.gloss: Five things make a country shine: riches, plentiful harvests, happiness, good health and security.

edges.reason: Gives five marks of a fine country, from health and wealth to happiness and safety.
edges.quote: five things are a country’s ornament

edges.reason: Wealth is one of the five things named.
edges.quote: wealth

edges.reason: A country wears its health, plenty and safety as an ornament.
edges.quote: a country’s ornament

couplets.gloss: A real country produces plenty without wearing its people out; one that gives only to endless toil hardly deserves the name.

edges.reason: Withholds the name of country from land that gives riches only when they are sought.
edges.quote: whose riches come without seeking

couplets.gloss: Even with all those blessings, a country is worth nothing without a good ruler.

edges.reason: Makes accord with the ruler the last test: without it, all a country’s gifts are of no use.
edges.quote: isn’t well matched with its ruler

edges.reason: Everything a land has is made to wait on the one who rules it.
edges.quote: its ruler

couplets.gloss: A fort is useful to those only trying to defend themselves, and just as useful to those strong enough to attack.

edges.reason: Says a fortress serves the strong and those who fear alike.
edges.quote: of value to those who are strong

couplets.gloss: Natural defences come in several forms: water, empty ground, hills and dense forest.

edges.reason: Counts water, open ground, hill and forest as the makings of a fortress.
edges.quote: water bright as a gem, open ground, a hill, and a forest of fine shade

couplets.gloss: The textbooks say a fort must be high, wide, solid and impossible to scale.

edges.reason: Cites the books for four tests of a fortress: height, breadth, strength and being hard to reach.
edges.quote: the books say a fortress is what has all four

couplets.gloss: The best fort has few weak spots to guard, plenty of room inside, and breaks the spirit of attackers.

edges.reason: Prefers little to guard and ample room, so that it breaks the spirit of whoever comes.
edges.quote: needs little guarding, has ample room

couplets.gloss: A fort must be hard to take, easy for its defenders to hold and well stocked with food.

edges.reason: Adds the garrison's side: easy to hold from within and full of food.
edges.quote: holds stores of food, and is easy for those inside to hold

couplets.gloss: A true fort holds everything it needs and has good people who will fight when it counts.

edges.reason: Wants full stores and good people who will help when the moment comes.
edges.quote: good people who help when the moment comes

couplets.gloss: A real fort cannot be taken by surrounding it, by storming it or by tunnelling under it.

edges.reason: Tests a fortress against three ways of taking it: encircling, attack and treachery within.
edges.quote: hard to take, whether by encircling it, by attacking without encircling, or by working treachery within

couplets.gloss: A true fort lets those inside beat the attackers, however hard they press.

edges.reason: Judges a fort by whether those inside can still win when the besiegers give everything.
edges.quote: hold fast and beat even those strong enough to surround it

couplets.gloss: A true fort is so well built that its defenders can bring enemies down right at the outer walls.

edges.reason: Looks for a fortress whose action fells the enemy at the very front of the fight.
edges.quote: the enemy falls at the very front of the fight

couplets.gloss: However good a fort is, it is no use if the people defending it do not act with spirit.

edges.reason: Even the finest fortress comes to nothing when those in it have no excellence in action.
edges.quote: with those who have no excellence in action it is no fortress

edges.reason: Treats vigour in the defenders as the thing that gives stone its worth.
edges.quote: vigour in action

couplets.gloss: Nothing else can turn a nobody into somebody the way money can.

edges.reason: Wealth alone can make someone of no account count for something.
edges.quote: makes people who don’t count into people who do

couplets.gloss: Everyone looks down on the poor, and everyone looks up to the rich.

edges.reason: Shows the honour wealth commands from everyone.
edges.quote: Everyone honours the rich

edges.reason: Shows what want costs a man: scorn from every side.
edges.quote: Everyone scorns those who have nothing

couplets.gloss: Money is a lamp that never lets you down: it lights up every dark corner wherever you take it.

edges.reason: Credits wealth with clearing the dark from wherever its owner goes.
edges.quote: goes to whatever land you think of and cuts through the dark

edges.reason: Pictures wealth as a lamp that never fails.
edges.quote: The unfailing lamp called wealth

edges.reason: Whatever wealth's light reaches stops being a dark place.
edges.quote: cuts through the dark

couplets.gloss: Money earned the right way, without doing wrong, brings both goodness and happiness.

edges.reason: Says both righteousness and happiness are born of wealth gained without wrong.
edges.quote: gives birth to righteousness and to happiness

edges.reason: Keeps its blessing for wealth that comes without wrong.
edges.quote: comes by knowing how, and without wrong

edges.reason: Names all three aims together, with honest wealth as the spring of the other two.
edges.quote: Wealth that comes by knowing how, and without wrong, gives birth to righteousness and to happiness

couplets.gloss: Do not go after money that comes without mercy or kindness; do not even touch it.

edges.reason: Makes compassion the condition wealth must meet before you embrace it.
edges.quote: Wealth that comes without compassion and loving-kindness

edges.reason: Bars a gain for how it comes, however great it may be.
edges.quote: don’t embrace it, let it roll away

couplets.gloss: A ruler's income comes from unclaimed estates, customs duties and what is taken from enemies.

edges.reason: Sets out where a ruler’s wealth comes from: what comes unbidden, customs dues and what he takes from enemies.
edges.quote: these are a ruler’s wealth

couplets.gloss: Compassion is love's child, and it needs money as a foster-mother to raise it.

edges.reason: Gives wealth a gentle task, tending compassion as a foster-mother tends a child.
edges.quote: the rich foster-mother called wealth

edges.reason: Places compassion in a family, born of loving-kindness and brought up by wealth.
edges.quote: Compassion, the child that loving-kindness bears

couplets.gloss: Starting a project with money behind you is like watching an elephant fight from a safe hilltop.

edges.reason: Wealth lets you take up a task as calmly as a spectator on a height.
edges.quote: Taking on a task with wealth in your hands

edges.reason: The hilltop is the safe place that wealth gives anyone who takes on a task.
edges.quote: from the top of a hill

edges.reason: The dangers of a task become a battle of elephants fought far below.
edges.quote: watching elephants fight

couplets.gloss: Build up your money: no blade is sharper for cutting an enemy's pride down to size.

edges.reason: Urges making wealth as the surest weapon against an enemy’s pride.
edges.quote: Make wealth

edges.reason: Wealth is steel, honed to cut through pride.
edges.quote: no steel sharper

couplets.gloss: Once you have built up plenty of wealth, the other two goals of life are easy to reach.

edges.reason: With bright wealth made in plenty, the other aims of life stay within easy reach.
edges.quote: made bright wealth in plenty

edges.reason: Counts wealth as the way to the other two aims of life.
edges.quote: the other two come easily, and together

couplets.gloss: A well-equipped, fearless, winning army is the most valuable thing a ruler owns.

edges.reason: Ranks a complete, winning army first among all a ruler owns.
edges.quote: the first of all a ruler’s riches

edges.reason: Asks of that army above all that it fear no wound.
edges.quote: fears no wound

edges.reason: Tells a ruler which of his riches counts for most.
edges.quote: a ruler’s riches

couplets.gloss: Only seasoned troops can stand firm in a desperate fight, whatever losses they take.

edges.reason: Prizes the hard courage that holds on when the fight goes badly.
edges.quote: hard courage that fears no wound

edges.reason: Singles out the old army as the only one that can do it.
edges.quote: rare except in an old army

couplets.gloss: However loudly a horde of rats squeals, one breath from a cobra finishes them.

edges.reason: Numbers and noise count for little: one cobra ends a whole host of rats.
edges.quote: A cobra breathes, and they are gone

edges.reason: One breath of the cobra stands for true force set against a weak crowd.
edges.quote: A cobra breathes

edges.reason: Gives the rats the roar of the ocean, only to show how little noise is worth.
edges.quote: roars like the sea

couplets.gloss: An army worthy of the name never breaks, cannot be bought and has courage in its history.

edges.reason: Keeps the name for a force undefeated, incorruptible and heir to a long tradition.
edges.quote: doesn’t fall, can’t be turned by treachery, and has hard courage handed down

couplets.gloss: A real army will stand together and face Death himself if he comes at it in a rage.

edges.reason: The test of an army is whether it would stand even against Death in his fury.
edges.quote: stand together and face even Death

edges.reason: Death comes on as a raging enemy for the ranks to meet.
edges.quote: Death, coming on in rage

couplets.gloss: Four things protect an army: bravery, honour, a clear mind and knowledge of the great wars before it.

edges.reason: Names what protects an army: valour, honour, the noble path and clarity of mind.
edges.quote: these four alone protect an army

edges.reason: Valour comes first among the four protections of an army.
edges.quote: Valour

edges.reason: Honour stands beside valour among the four protections of an army.
edges.quote: honour

edges.reason: Clarity of mind is counted among the four things that protect an army.
edges.quote: clarity of mind

couplets.gloss: A true army charges at the enemy, confident it can withstand whatever comes when battle is joined.

edges.reason: Makes going forward the mark of an army, since it knows how to bear the fight that comes.
edges.quote: holds back the vanguard and goes forward

couplets.gloss: Even an army short on fighting spirit and staying power can make up for it with superior equipment.
An army wins as long as it is not too small, is not eaten up by feuds and is not left unpaid.

edges.reason: Victory rests on three things: no shrinking, no lasting grudge and no poverty.
edges.quote: no shrinking, no grudge that won’t go, and no poverty

couplets.gloss: Plenty of troops does not make an army if there are no leaders to command them.

edges.reason: However many men stand in line, it takes leaders to make them an army.
edges.quote: without leaders it is no army

edges.reason: Makes the leader the one person an army can’t do without.
edges.quote: without leaders

couplets.gloss: Enemies, do not stand against my chief: many who did are memorial stones now.
couplets.sensitive: boasts of men killed in battle

edges.reason: Boasts that those who stood before this lord now stand in stone.
edges.quote: Many have stood before him, and now they stand in stone

edges.reason: A soldier's boast on his master's behalf shows where his devotion lies.
edges.quote: don’t stand before my lord

edges.reason: Shouts its warning straight at the foe.
edges.quote: Enemies

couplets.gloss: A spear thrown at an elephant that misses is more glorious than an arrow that hits a rabbit.

edges.reason: A throw at a great target that misses outranks a hit on a small one.
edges.quote: Better to hold a spear that missed an elephant

edges.reason: The elephant is the great target worth failing at.
edges.quote: a spear that missed an elephant

edges.reason: The spear is a bold effort, measured by its aim and not by its success.
edges.quote: hold a spear

edges.reason: Tells someone who aimed high and missed that the miss still beats a small success.
edges.quote: a spear that missed an elephant

couplets.gloss: Fierce courage is what people call bravery, but being generous to someone who is down is what gives it its cutting edge.

edges.reason: Says what great manhood is, then what sharpens it: generosity when someone falls on hard times.
edges.quote: They call fierce courage great manhood

edges.reason: Praises generosity to someone in trouble as what gives courage its edge.
edges.quote: generosity is the sharp edge of it

couplets.gloss: A warrior who has thrown his spear at an elephant finds another in his own body and pulls it out with a smile.
couplets.sensitive: delights in being wounded in battle

edges.reason: The wound is forgotten, and the spear in his body is only a welcome new weapon.
edges.quote: pulls it out and laughs

edges.reason: Tells the story of one fighting man in the thick of battle.
edges.quote: He lets the spear in his hand go with an elephant

couplets.gloss: Isn't it a disgrace to a brave man if he so much as blinks when a spear is thrown at him?

edges.reason: Even a blink at a thrown spear counts as running away.
edges.quote: a glaring eye blinks

edges.reason: Sets the fighting man's own standard of disgrace.
edges.quote: for those with hard courage

couplets.gloss: A brave fighter counts any day without a serious wound as a day wasted.
couplets.sensitive: praises being wounded; could reach someone who self-harms

edges.reason: A day without a noble wound is written off as lost.
edges.quote: every day with no noble wound

edges.reason: Gives the fighting man's own reckoning of a day well spent.
edges.quote: He counts over his days

couplets.gloss: Men who do not care for their lives and want fame that spreads across the world wear the warrior's anklet beautifully.
couplets.sensitive: praises giving up one’s life for fame

edges.reason: Those who don’t want life make even their anklet an ornament.
edges.quote: don’t want life

edges.reason: Fame that circles the world is what these warriors give their lives to earn.
edges.quote: fame that circles the world

couplets.gloss: Brave soldiers who do not fear for their lives keep their discipline even when their commander turns harsh on them.

edges.reason: Good soldiers hold to their duty even when their chief turns severe.
edges.quote: they forget not their discipline even when their chief is severe upon them

edges.reason: Speaks of warriors who don’t fear for their lives.
edges.quote: Warriors who don’t fear for their lives

edges.reason: Names the anger of the ruler who leads them as the trial of these warriors.
edges.quote: even if the ruler is angry with them

couplets.gloss: Who could blame people who die trying to do what they vowed to do?
couplets.sensitive: could read as approving of dying for a cause

edges.reason: Holds those who die rather than break their vow to be beyond all blame.
edges.quote: die rather than go back on their vow

couplets.gloss: A death that brings tears to your leader's eyes is worth begging for.

edges.reason: A death that fills the eyes of those who cared for you is worth begging for.
edges.quote: that death is worth begging for

edges.reason: Measures the warrior’s death by what it makes those who cared for him feel.
edges.quote: those who cared for you

couplets.gloss: Nothing is harder to gain than real friendship, and nothing protects you better from those working against you.

edges.reason: Calls friendship the hardest thing to make and the hardest guard to get past.
edges.quote: What is as hard to make as friendship

couplets.gloss: Friendship with good people grows like the waxing moon; friendship with fools shrinks like the waning one.

edges.reason: Gives the bond with worthy men the steady growth of the moon.
edges.quote: The friendship of the worthy fills out like the new moon

edges.reason: Sets the moon's waxing and waning side by side to sort good bonds from bad.
edges.quote: fills out like the new moon

couplets.gloss: The company of good people is like a great book: the more you go back to it, the more you enjoy it.

edges.reason: Good friends, like great books, keep showing fresh charm the closer one comes.
edges.quote: each time you return to it, it delights you more

couplets.gloss: Friendship is not there for the laughs; it is there to pull you up sharply when you go wrong.

edges.reason: Says its purpose is not fun but the checking of one who strays.
edges.quote: not to laugh together

edges.reason: Makes reproof of a straying friend the very point of the bond.
edges.quote: to step in and rebuke when someone goes too far

edges.reason: Someone stung by a friend's rebuke is told that this is what friendship is for.
edges.quote: step in and rebuke

couplets.gloss: You do not need to see each other all the time: shared feeling is what makes friends close.

edges.reason: Puts the strength of friendship in shared feeling, not in hours spent together.
edges.quote: Feeling alone gives the bond of friendship

couplets.gloss: Smiling at someone does not make you their friend; real friendship is gladness deep in the heart.

edges.reason: Separates the smile on the face from the smile deep in the heart.
edges.quote: Friendship that makes the face smile is not friendship

couplets.gloss: A real friend steers you away from doing wrong, points you to what is right and shares your troubles when things fall apart.

edges.reason: Gives three marks of friendship: it turns you from ruin, sets you on the path and shares the pain.
edges.quote: Friendship turns you from what would ruin you

edges.reason: Credits friendship with turning you from ruin and setting you on the path.
edges.quote: turns you from what would ruin you, sets you on the path

edges.reason: Sets out what anyone called a friend must do for you.
edges.quote: shares the pain when ruin comes

couplets.gloss: A true friend rushes to help you in trouble, as quickly as your hand grabs at clothing that is slipping off.

edges.reason: Friendship is a reflex here, as quick as a hand saving a slipping garment.
edges.quote: friendship takes away trouble on the spot

edges.reason: Pictures what the true friend does without stopping to think.
edges.quote: takes away trouble on the spot

edges.reason: Gives the rule for a friend's crisis: move at once, as a hand moves to a slipping cloth.
edges.quote: Like the hand of someone whose clothes slip

couplets.gloss: Friendship is at its best when two people stay steady with each other and prop each other up however they can.

edges.reason: Places friendship’s throne in unwavering support, given in every way it can.
edges.quote: Where does friendship sit enthroned

couplets.gloss: A friendship that keeps score of who loves whom and how much is a poor thing, however proudly it is described.

edges.reason: A bond that is spelled out and praised looks poor for all the praise.
edges.quote: Say it, however finely, and the friendship looks poor

couplets.gloss: Nothing is worse than making a friend without checking them out first, because a good person cannot walk away afterwards.

edges.reason: Calls friendship without trial the worst ill, since the loyal man cannot undo it.
edges.quote: Nothing ruins you like making friends without looking into them

edges.reason: Warns anyone opening up to a new person to test first, because the tie is hard to undo.
edges.quote: once made there is no leaving it

couplets.gloss: If you keep making friends without looking into them carefully, you will end up with sorrow that lasts until you die.

edges.reason: Friends taken on without trial bring trouble that lasts to the grave.
edges.quote: makes a friend without looking and looking again

couplets.gloss: Before you become someone's friend, look at their family, their good and bad points and the people they mix with.

edges.reason: Lays out what to weigh: character, family, faults and the kin around them.
edges.quote: Know a person’s character, family, faults and the unfailing kin around them

edges.reason: Gives a checklist for anyone deciding whether a new person deserves their trust.
edges.quote: then make them your friend

couplets.gloss: It is worth paying to make a friend of someone from a decent family who would be ashamed to do wrong.

edges.reason: Good family is one of the two marks of a friend worth paying for.
edges.quote: Someone well-born

edges.reason: Shrinking from blame is what makes such a friend worth paying for.
edges.quote: shrinks from blame upon himself

couplets.gloss: Look for friends who know what is right and who will tell you off, even to tears, when you go wrong.

edges.reason: Tells you to seek out as friends the very people who will rebuke you.
edges.quote: can speak until you weep, rebuke you

edges.reason: Tells someone smarting from correction that such correctors are the friends to keep.
edges.quote: Choose with care friends who, when you go wrong, can speak until you weep

couplets.gloss: There is one good thing about disaster: it shows you exactly how far your friends will go.

edges.reason: Finds one gain in ruin: it measures who your own people are.
edges.quote: Even in ruin there is one benefit

edges.reason: Ruin is the rod laid against each of your people to take their true length.
edges.quote: a rod that measures your people to their full length

edges.reason: Turns the loss of friends in bad times into a measure of what they ever were.
edges.quote: a rod that measures your people

couplets.gloss: Getting rid of a foolish friend is a real gain.

edges.reason: Counts giving up a fool's friendship as clear profit.
edges.quote: give up the friendship of fools

couplets.gloss: Do not dwell on things that shrink your spirit, and do not befriend people who would leave you when you are in trouble.

edges.reason: Warns off those who cut away your strength the moment you are in trouble.
edges.quote: those who cut away your strength in trouble

couplets.gloss: Even on your deathbed, the memory of friends who deserted you in disaster will burn.

edges.reason: The memory of friends who failed in disaster still burns at the hour of death.
edges.quote: burns the heart, even if you think of it when death is upon you

couplets.gloss: Seek out the friendship of good people, and shake off unworthy ones even if you have to give them something to go away.

edges.reason: Urges holding to the spotless and leaving those who don’t fit, whatever that costs.
edges.quote: Cling to the friendship of the spotless

edges.reason: Says to get clear of unworthy friends even if it takes a parting gift.
edges.quote: Give something if you must, and leave the friendship of those who don’t fit

couplets.gloss: Old friendship means accepting whatever liberties the other takes, without any resentment.
couplets.sensitive: urges submitting without resentment to a loved one’s liberties

edges.reason: Defines old friendship as the kind that in no way cuts back the rights of closeness.
edges.quote: friendship that in no way cuts back the rights of closeness

couplets.gloss: Being relaxed and informal with each other is the core of friendship, and good people never take offence at it.

edges.reason: Makes the rights of closeness a limb of friendship itself.
edges.quote: The rights of closeness are a limb of friendship

couplets.gloss: What is a long friendship worth if it cannot go along with the liberties friends take?
couplets.sensitive: presses one to accept whatever liberties a friend takes

edges.reason: Asks what years of friendship are for if they will not allow such liberties.
edges.quote: What use is long friendship

couplets.gloss: When friends use their closeness to do something without asking, people with warm hearts remember the love and take it well.

edges.reason: A friend’s unasked act, done out of closeness, is welcomed as something to wish for.
edges.quote: act without asking, people welcome it

edges.reason: Concerns how one friend should take what another does unasked.
edges.quote: When friends, out of closeness, act without asking

edges.reason: For a friend who overstepped: recall the love and let the act pass.
edges.quote: take it in good part

couplets.gloss: When a friend does something that hurts you, put it down either to how close you are or to plain ignorance.
couplets.sensitive: tells the hurt to explain away a friend’s harm

edges.reason: Would have a friend's hurtful act read as closeness as much as ignorance.
edges.quote: foolishness or to great closeness

edges.reason: Tells one friend how to read the pain another has caused.
edges.quote: If friends do something that hurts

edges.reason: Offers someone wounded by a friend two gentler readings of what happened.
edges.quote: put it down to foolishness or to great closeness

couplets.gloss: A true friend will not give up a long friendship even when that friend has brought them to ruin.
couplets.sensitive: praises staying with someone who ruined you

edges.reason: Even ruin does not end the bond for those who keep to the bounds of friendship.
edges.quote: don’t leave those who have stood by them from of old, even in ruin

couplets.gloss: People whose love goes back a long way keep loving a friend even when that friend keeps doing them harm.
couplets.sensitive: praises loving on through repeated harm

edges.reason: Long loving-kindness does not slacken, even when a friend does ruinous things.
edges.quote: don’t lose their loving-kindness

couplets.gloss: For those who will not hear a word against a friend, the day that friend wrongs them is a day to celebrate.
couplets.sensitive: calls a friend’s injury a cause for celebration

edges.reason: So deep is the closeness that the day a friend does wrong becomes a good day.
edges.quote: the day the friend does wrong is a good day

couplets.gloss: People who never let go of a friendship that has lasted are loved by everyone.

edges.reason: Not giving up an old friend wins the desire of the whole world.
edges.quote: The world desires those who don’t give up

couplets.gloss: Those who do not change towards their old friends earn warmth even from their enemies.

edges.reason: Constancy to old friends softens even those who wish one harm.
edges.quote: desired even by those who don’t desire them

couplets.gloss: Worthless people may act as if they cannot get enough of you, but it is better when such a friendship fades than when it grows.

edges.reason: A show of devouring fondness from those without character is best seen shrinking.
edges.quote: better shrinking than growing

couplets.gloss: Why care whether you keep or lose people who stick around when it pays and leave when it does not?
keywords: only call when they need something

edges.reason: Describes friends who fawn while it pays and leave when the profit stops.
edges.quote: make friends when it pays and leave when it doesn’t

edges.reason: Asks someone deserted what such a friendship was ever worth.
edges.quote: what does it matter if you gain or lose them

couplets.gloss: People who are friends only for what they can get are in the same class as thieves and those who take money for love.

edges.reason: Ranks the friend who weighs the gain with thieves and those who take what they are paid.
edges.quote: Friends who weigh what they stand to gain

couplets.gloss: Some people are like an untrained horse that throws you in battle and bolts: better to be alone than have them as friends.

edges.reason: Prefers being alone to friends who fail you in the fight like an untaught horse.
edges.quote: Better to be alone

couplets.gloss: Better to have no friendship at all with low people who leave you when you need them.
keywords: no friends better than bad friends

edges.reason: Says friends who forsake one at the moment of need are better never had.
edges.quote: give no protection even when you have made it

edges.reason: Reassures the one forsaken that not having such friends is the better state.
edges.quote: better not had than had

couplets.gloss: Being on bad terms with wise people is ten million times better than being close to a fool.

edges.reason: Rates a fool's closeness so low that the hostility of the wise beats it ten million times.
edges.quote: the deepest friendship of a fool

couplets.gloss: An enemy's hatred is worth far more than the friendship of people who only want to laugh and flatter.

edges.reason: Puts friends who are only for laughter below enemies by a hundred million times.
edges.quote: a friendship that is only laughter

couplets.gloss: Say nothing to friends who get in the way of what you are doing; just let the friendship slowly drop.

edges.reason: A friend who spoils your work earns only a slow and silent letting go.
edges.quote: say nothing, and let the friendship slowly slip away

couplets.gloss: Keeping company with people whose actions do not match their words is bitter, even in a dream.
keywords: saying one thing and doing another

edges.reason: A friend whose deeds belie his words is bitter even to remember in sleep.
edges.quote: whose acts are one thing and words another

couplets.gloss: Keep well away from those who are nice to you in private but run you down in public.

edges.reason: Sets warmth at home against blame in the assembly.
edges.quote: warm at home and blame you in the assembly

edges.reason: Gives one flat rule for those who are warm in private and blame you in public: keep away.
edges.quote: come near you at all

couplets.gloss: An enemy's pretended friendship is just the anvil they will use to strike you when the chance comes.

edges.reason: Turns the friendship of those not with you at heart into an anvil on which you will be struck.
edges.quote: is an anvil

edges.reason: Looks at what friendship means in the hands of someone who is an enemy at heart.
edges.quote: those who keep company without agreeing at heart

couplets.gloss: Those who act like friends while being enemies at heart will turn on you without warning.

edges.reason: Seems your own, is not, and will change when the chance comes.
edges.quote: those who seem your own but are not

couplets.gloss: However much good study an enemy does, it is very hard for them to become good-hearted.

edges.reason: Hate in an enemy’s heart outlasts even much good learning.
edges.quote: hard for enemies to become good at heart

edges.reason: Warns that a learned foe is still a foe.
edges.quote: Even after learning many good things

couplets.gloss: Be afraid of deceitful people who smile at you while their heart is full of spite.

edges.reason: Warns to fear the smile that covers bitterness within.
edges.quote: smile sweetly with the face and are bitter within

edges.reason: Tells someone facing a smiling opponent plainly to be afraid of him.
edges.quote: Fear the deceivers

couplets.gloss: Do not rely in any way on the words of people who are not with you at heart.

edges.reason: Words from those whose minds are not with you deserve no trust at all.
edges.quote: not to be trusted in anything, on their words alone

couplets.gloss: Even when an enemy talks kindly like a friend, it soon becomes clear what they really are.

edges.reason: Good words, spoken as friends speak, can’t hide the hostile speaker for long.
edges.quote: soon seen for what they are

edges.reason: Says how quickly the foe shows through his words.
edges.quote: the words of those who aren’t with you

couplets.gloss: Do not trust an enemy's humble words: a bow bends only to do harm.

edges.reason: Bowing speech from an enemy is a threat and not a courtesy.
edges.quote: the bowing words of enemies

edges.reason: The bowing of his speech is compared to a bow bending to shoot.
edges.quote: The bowing of a bow means harm

edges.reason: Concerns the enemy who comes with bowing speech.
edges.quote: Don’t trust the bowing words of enemies

couplets.gloss: An enemy may hide a weapon in hands folded in respect, and their tears are no more to be trusted.

edges.reason: Even a gesture of reverence may have a weapon inside it.
edges.quote: A weapon hides in the joined hands of enemies

edges.reason: An enemy’s weeping is one more disguise for a hidden weapon.
edges.quote: in their tears too

edges.reason: Watches an enemy’s hands and tears for what they hide.
edges.quote: the joined hands of enemies

couplets.gloss: With people who praise you in public and mock you in private, keep them happy to their face while destroying them from within the friendship.
couplets.sensitive: urges secretly crushing those who mock you

edges.reason: Describes those who make much of you outwardly and despise you all the same.
edges.quote: make much of you and despise you

couplets.gloss: When you cannot yet break with an enemy, act friendly on the surface but keep them out of your heart.

edges.reason: Counsels a false front towards an enemy who turns friend, until you can drop it.
edges.quote: be friends with the face, and put friendship out of the heart

ideaLinks.reason: Learning by the right path is given as the way to answer unafraid in any assembly.
ideaLinks.quote: Learn by the right path and know the measure, so that you can answer in an assembly without fear

ideaLinks.reason: A strong fortress is named among the limbs of a country.
ideaLinks.quote: a strong fortress are the limbs of a country

ideaLinks.reason: Rainwater is named among the things no country can do without.
ideaLinks.quote: rainwater, well-situated mountains, and strong fortifications, these are indispensable to every country

ideaLinks.reason: All of a country’s gifts come to nothing unless it is well matched with its ruler.
ideaLinks.quote: a country is of no use if it isn’t well matched with its ruler

ideaLinks.reason: However strong the walls, they avail nothing without vigour in those who hold them.
ideaLinks.quote: it will avail nothing if the defenders show not vigour in action

ideaLinks.reason: Wealth gained without wrong gives birth to righteousness.
Compassion needs wealth as a child needs a foster-mother to raise it.
ideaLinks.quote: thrives with the rich foster-mother called wealth

ideaLinks.reason: Compassion is called the child of loving-kindness.
No steel cuts a foe's pride as sharply as wealth does.
ideaLinks.quote: no sharper steel to cleave thy foeman’s pride

ideaLinks.reason: Without leaders, steadfast men however many are no army.
ideaLinks.quote: without leaders it is no army

proposals.label: The Watered Plant
proposals.why: Water at the root of a growing plant recurs as a figure for what nourishes or starves; the guide itself cites 1304, but no image entry covers it.
